Contributing

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Keep changes reviewable and include tests for changed behavior. Integration tests must install cdrgam and cdrgam.cli into a clean temporary library and exercise only exported core APIs. Generated project state and package build artifacts do not belong in version control.

Use the narrowest applicable test scope while developing:

./scripts/test architecture
./scripts/test cli
./scripts/test paths
./scripts/test registry
./scripts/test identities
./scripts/test integration
./scripts/test portability

Development scripts resolve R through the active Conda environment first. If none is active, they use the cdrgam Conda environment when it exists. Set CDRGAM_CONDA_ENV to choose a different environment or R_BIN to select an exact executable. Local scripts otherwise fail rather than silently choosing a system R; CDRGAM_ALLOW_SYSTEM_R=1 is an explicit override. Hosted checks continue to use their provisioned R.

./scripts/test all runs every scope. Each invocation installs the current CLI source into a temporary library. The integration scope covers the complete project lifecycle and is reserved for changes that cross component boundaries. The portability scope also checks the cross-platform preflight selection policy and is appropriate after changes to paths, launchers, process handling, or scheduler integration.

Development branches are not release-gated. Before opening a release pull request, run the manual cross-platform preflight when changes may affect paths, file I/O, launchers, process handling, scheduler integration, or runtime configuration:

gh workflow run cross-platform-preflight.yaml --ref dev -f scope=auto
gh run watch

The preflight compares the selected commit with the newest successful automatic or full preflight ancestor on that branch. If no such run exists, it uses the merge base with main. It runs the Windows, macOS, and Linux portability profile only when the cumulative un-preflighted changes match the policy. Use scope=full to force complete package checks. A narrow manual scope does not advance the automatic baseline.

Keep calls to cdrgam and knowledge of fitted-object representation in R/core-adapter.R. Keep SQLite access in R/registry.R. The architecture test enforces these boundaries. Add a public core API when the adapter lacks a required operation; do not inspect an additional core implementation field in another CLI module.

Before proposing a release, update Version in DESCRIPTION and document intentional schema or command-line incompatibilities and their migration path. The hosted release gate is the authoritative clean-environment check.

Run the repository’s correctness-focused R lint profile after installing the package and its dependencies:

"$(./scripts/r-bin)" -e 'lintr::lint_package(".")'

The profile preserves the established formatting conventions. New lint rules should identify actionable defects without requiring unrelated restyling.

Material AI assistance must be disclosed in affected commits with an Assisted-by: <tool-or-agent>:<model-identifier> trailer. A human contributor remains the author and is responsible for review. Do not invent or modify Git identity, substitute another account, fabricate a signature, or add a Signed-off-by: certification without explicit human authorization.

Commits, pushes, tags, pull requests, and releases require an explicit user request. Technical prose must follow WRITING_POLICY.md.

Releases and compatibility

main contains released code. Prepare releases on dev or a release branch and merge them into main only through a pull request. Every pull request to main must change Version in DESCRIPTION to a later MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH value. Repository protection requires the release gate and the Linux, macOS, and Windows package checks to pass before merge. The release gate runs the lint profile, the complete test suite through R CMD check, and the complete pkgdown build against the released core package.

Use patch releases for compatible fixes. During the 0.x series, use minor releases for new features and intentional interface changes. Release the core package first when a harness release requires a newer core API.

After the pull request merges, create an annotated vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag on the validated merge commit, using a concise summary written for that release, not generated by a script or template, as the tag message. The tag workflow rejects versions that do not match DESCRIPTION, lightweight or empty tags, and commits outside main, then uses that message as the corresponding GitHub Release description. Verify the tag workflow and final description before treating publication as complete. Never move or replace a published tag.
